title: A Radio Segment on Living Under One Roof Across Generations
script: Host: [thoughtful] Tonight we're discussing the resurgence of multigenerational households, families choosing to live under one roof across three generations rather than scattering into separate homes. On the line is Yusuf.
Caller: Thank you for having me. This arrangement isn't new for my family exactly, but it's certainly become more deliberate over the past few years.
Host: [carefully] Tell us how it actually came together for you.
Caller: My father's health declined gradually, and rather than moving him into assisted living, we renovated our garage into a small, self-contained unit where he could live independently but nearby.
Host: [reflective] What prompted that particular choice over the more conventional options available?
Caller: Partly cultural, partly practical. But mostly, I couldn't reconcile the idea of outsourcing his final years to strangers when we had the physical space to do otherwise.
Host: [honestly] Was the adjustment as straightforward as that decision might sound in hindsight?
Caller: Not remotely. The first year involved considerable friction, mostly around autonomy, my father resented feeling supervised, and I resented feeling perpetually on call.
Host: [gently] How did you navigate that friction?
Caller: We eventually set explicit boundaries, agreed hours where we weren't checking on him, agreed signals for when he genuinely needed help versus simply wanted company.
Host: [calmly] So structure, rather than simply proximity, made the arrangement sustainable?
Caller: Entirely. Proximity without structure just produces resentment on both sides, dressed up as devotion.
Host: [encouraging] What would you say to families considering this but worried about losing their own independence?

Caller: I'd say the independence you're protecting is often overrated compared to what you gain, my children now know their grandfather intimately, not as an occasional visitor but as someone woven into daily life.
Host: [seriously] A trade worth making, in your view?
Caller: Genuinely, yes, though I'd never claim it's the right arrangement for every family. It simply happened to be right for ours.
Host: Thank you, Yusuf, for such an honest window into a decision more families are quietly reconsidering.
Caller: Thank you for giving it real airtime instead of treating it as a nostalgic curiosity.
